name: Brazilian nationalism
summary: Brazilian nationalism holds that Brazil is a single, racially and culturally blended nation whose independence and prosperity depend on a strong, centralizing state. In its twentieth-century mainstream, the Vargas-era and developmentalist tradition, it pairs state-led industrialization and economic sovereignty (import substitution, state firms, an oil monopoly) with labour protection through a corporatist state and a pride in miscegenation, while resisting foreign economic influence.
scope: The mainstream twentieth-century nationalist-developmentalist tradition: Getulio Vargas's 1930-45 and 1951-54 governments (Estado Novo, CLT, Petrobras), the 1950s ISEB intellectuals, and Gilberto Freyre's racial-democracy cultural nationalism. It excludes Integralism as a separate fascist movement and contemporary Bolsonarist right-wing nationalism. Many answers are inferred, since the sources document economic, labour, centralist and cultural positions but rarely social or technological ones.

keyFigures.name: Getulio Vargas
keyFigures.role: President who built the Estado Novo and the state-led nationalist economy (CSN, Petrobras, CLT).

keyFigures.name: Gilberto Freyre
keyFigures.role: Sociologist whose Casa-Grande & Senzala systematized the ideal of a racially mixed nation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from the Vargas-era creation of a Ministry of Education and Health and social-protection ethos; healthcare provision itself is not a documented plank.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Vargas created the minimum wage in the Estado Novo and his farewell letter defends the revision of the minimum wage against the hatred it provoked.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nationalists backed import substitution and state firms (CSN, Vale, Petrobras) because they distrusted letting the market alone decide Brazil's industrial future.

public-ownership.rationale: The state built CSN and Vale and held a Petrobras oil monopoly; the "oil is ours" campaign made public ownership of strategic sectors a nationalist emblem.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred: Vargas's letter cites the stalled extraordinary-profits law, implying support for taxing windfall profits, though broad wealth taxation is not documented.

unions-good.rationale: Vargas courted workers through the CLT and official unions, but as state-supervised bodies, so approval is qualified.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: nationalists subordinated property to national interest (state monopolies, profit-remittance limits), though they were not anti-capitalist.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Vargas's letter denounces foreign firms' profits of up to 500% a year and fraud in import declarations, favouring tighter control of (especially foreign) corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: The movement's labour-protection legacy (CLT, minimum wage, "father of the poor") stands against cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: ISEB envisioned a capitalist national revolution with workers allied to a national bourgeoisie, not worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the Estado Novo's security-state practices and anti-communism; not a documented doctrinal point.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the regime's moralizing, hierarchical social conservatism; drugs are not discussed in the sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split: racial-democracy nationalism denies racism exists, yet the state has policed speech by decree; no clear doctrine.

strong-leader.rationale: The Estado Novo and its 1937 constitution concentrated power in the president, and propaganda cast Vargas as the father of the poor and nation.

state-harmful.rationale: Nationalism relies on a strong state to build industry and unify the nation, so it rejects the view of the state as harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Estado Novo favoured state arms monopoly while Brazilian right nationalists oppose limits, so adherents split.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Estado Novo modernized the armed forces (Air Force, military academy) and the army backed the oil campaign for national security.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the regime's conservative Catholic-leaning moral outlook; not discussed in sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Vargas replaced governors with federal intervenors, burned state flags and said "we no longer have regional problems", all are national.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not documented; the regime was repressive toward political prisoners but nothing indicates a stance on penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: The 1937 constitution had a chapter on the family and the regime blended hierarchical, Catholic-conservative values.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the regime's conservative social values; anachronistic for the movement's peak.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the regime's closeness to the Catholic Church; not documented as an issue.

more-religion-public.rationale: Vargas drew closer to the Catholic Church and allowed religion in public schools, though the state stayed formally secular.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial-democracy nationalism holds Brazil largely escaped racism, so it historically resisted race-conscious correction; resistance to quotas is noted.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the regime's hierarchical conservative outlook; not discussed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural nationalism, from Alencar's literature to the Estado Novo's nationalization campaign, centres on defending an authentic Brazilian culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Split: Vargas claimed revolution in 1930 and 1937 yet kept elites and institutions; no doctrinal stance.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Vargas limited immigration and required two-thirds Brazilian workers in factories; the nationalization campaign aimed to integrate immigrants.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sovereignty and resistance to international financial groups mark the tradition, making expanded international authority unwelcome.

free-trade.rationale: Import substitution and protection of domestic industry were core economic nationalist policy.

nation-first.rationale: Vargas's letter frames foreign groups as despoiling Brazil, and the oil monopoly excluded foreign capital; national interest comes first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; neutrality and sovereignty favour no, but Brazil sent troops (FEB) to the Allied war effort.

open-borders.rationale: Immigration was limited and immigrants nationalized; open borders runs against the nationalist project.

limit-growth.rationale: ISEB defined development as industrialization to sustain income growth, the opposite of limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the growth-first developmentalism; climate not discussed in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from the faith in industrialization and modernization as the path to national development.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the developmentalist drive for energy and technology self-sufficiency; not documented.

revolution-justified.rationale: Vargas called himself leader of a revolution (1930) yet nationalism spans both revolutionary and order-defending strands.

experts-over-public.rationale: ISEB placed the state bureaucracy at the head of nation-building; technocratic leaning is inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Nationalists favoured state-led industrial planning within a capitalist framework, not full central planning; split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not their model: ISEB sought a national capitalist revolution, but state ownership was accepted in strategic sectors.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition favoured work-linked protection (CLT, minimum wage) over unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Import substitution industrialization behind protection was the central economic policy of Vargas-era nationalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state created CSN, Vale, CNP and Petrobras and ISEB made the state bureaucracy a lead agent of industrialization.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not a documented plank; strand focused on national industry, not property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labour was protected through the CLT and the minimum wage; abolition is alien to the tradition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from the statist stance; nationalists favoured state control of finance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Estado Novo recognized class organizations, official unions, labour courts, and a corporatist structure in the 1937 constitution.

one-party-rule.rationale: Vargas despised parties and abolished them rather than build a single ruling party, though he said the single party would fragment.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The elite relied on the monarchy only early; the republican nationalism of the Vargas era did not favour hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Split: Vargas ruled as dictator 1937-45 but was elected in 1950, and later nationalists (PTB) stressed electoral politics.

direct-votes.rationale: Not documented; the 1937 constitution promised a plebiscite that was never held.

workers-councils.rationale: The regime brought unions under state control and rejected class-based autonomous power structures.

right-to-secede.rationale: Vargas stressed national unity and abolished state autonomy, burning state flags.

natural-rulers.rationale: The regime drew on Castilhism, which held rulers should be chosen for moral purity, though adherents rarely state this as natural fitness.

political-violence-never.rationale: The tradition included revolt (1930, tenentismo) and repressive policies; the stance is inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not documented; militarism was present but no doctrinal claim.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1937 constitution kept laicity yet the state cooperated with the Church and allowed religion in schools.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laicity was retained in the 1937 constitution; laws were not derived from scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Nationalist statism rejects privatizing courts, policing, and defence; armed forces were state institutions.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the regime's strengthening of the armed forces and the army's security rationale.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Brazilian nationalism defines the nation as a fusion of indigenous, African, and European cultures, not a single ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The regime treated class struggle as something to be denied or managed through corporatist collaboration.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Vargas defended workers and the humble, but redistribution toward equal outcomes is not stated.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist state centralized authority; indigenous land authority is not discussed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Nationalism arose against Portuguese rule, but reparations are not addressed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalism is Brazil-centred; Latin American or Lusophone union is not a documented plank in the sources.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Vargas framed himself as serving the people against selfish foreign and domestic interests; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Vargas stated "Individuals don't have rights, they have duties!"

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; developmentalism viewed natural wealth as resources for national power.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from the developmentalist and nationalist valuation of national population and growth.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: ISEB and Vargas treated industrialization as the path out of a "semi-colonial, agrarian" condition.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Modernization was prized, but not at the expense of institutions; split.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the regime's security-state approach.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nationalists were oriented to development and modernization, not restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: ISEB's pragmatic development framing and Vargas's flexible policy shifts suggest pragmatism; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: The regime preferred state-led change, though the 1930 revolution was extra-electoral.

means-match-ends.rationale: No source addresses whether methods must mirror ends; the regime used authoritarian means for a developmental end, but adherents are not documented either way.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to a hunter-gatherer return; the tradition prizes industrial modernization.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Industrialization as a goal implies the division of labour is retained.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Social protection of workers is central, but distribution by need is not stated.

production-for-use.rationale: ISEB envisioned capitalist national development with profit-seeking firms.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Vargas condemned foreign firms' profits of up to 500%, but not profit in general as exploitation; split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-communism was a pillar; the regime banned the Communist Party.

collective-farming.rationale: Anti-communist and landowner-accommodating regime rejected collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: ISEB sought national capitalist development; the thesis is not stated.

taxation-theft.rationale: A statist developmentalist tradition rejects this libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: The regime restricted conduct for national and moral reasons beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Vargas's "individuals don't have rights, they have duties" rejects rights-only individualism.

conscription.rationale: The regime strengthened the military and applied selection criteria to conscripts.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalism ties the citizen to the nation; exit is not valued.

state-as-business.rationale: The tradition views the state as a national guardian, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Vargas spoke of "social freedom" and freeing workers from dependence, a materially grounded notion of liberty.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not documented, though the regime controlled media itself via the DIP.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial democracy ideology, drawn from Freyre, emphasized culture and miscegenation; though early whitening theory is noted, the mainstream rejected hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1937 constitution and regime recognized class organizations and the Council of National Economy as corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: The Estado Novo regime directed culture, press, education, and the economy, though it fell short of totalitarian; fascist-inspired.

national-rebirth.rationale: Vargas cast the Estado Novo as a break with a "semi-colonial, agrarian" past and the old liberal order.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Brazilian nationalism is defensive and developmental, not irredentist; neutrality marked foreign policy.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule rested on a constitution and bureaucratic state, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The regime enacted labour protection; bound labour is alien.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from the regime's ideological control of education and media; not a stated epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred from the regime's Catholic-conservative moral tone.

single-common-good.rationale: Corporatist thought presents a unitary national interest above class conflict.

revive-national-language.rationale: Portuguese is the established language, not a lapsed one; question barely applies.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporatism mediated labour through state bodies, not workplace votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: the regime centralized and nationalized education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Developmentalists accepted deficits and state investment, though ISEB warned about foreign debt.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: nationalists subordinated economic liberty to state direction.

rule-by-example.rationale: Castilhism emphasized rulers' moral purity as the basis of authority.

national-self-determination.rationale: Brazilian nationalism arose from the demand for independence from Portugal and a unified self-governing nation.

force-without-un.rationale: No documented position; sovereignty stance versus modest military role.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Inferred from the closeness to Catholic conservatism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Vargas-era labour rights, minimum wage and two-thirds Brazilian workforce rule favoured nationals.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the work-centred CLT model in which entitlements attached to formal employment.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Estado Novo described itself in terms of collaboration among classes through corporatist bodies, denying class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural nationalism values inherited national culture, from Alencar's literary nationalism onwards.

dominated-front.rationale: Vargas's anti-international-group stance suggests sympathy, but formal fronts with other dominated countries are not documented.

workers-nation.rationale: Vargas incorporated workers into national politics through state-linked unions and the CLT rather than international class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical and Catholic-conservative values of the regime.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a plank; ISEB's developmentalism worked within capitalist finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Brazilian nationalism took pride in contrasting racial democracy with US segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The corporatist state presented itself as above classes, not a tool of one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The "oil is ours" campaign and Petrobras monopoly aimed to develop domestic oil production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Estado Novo nationalization campaign banned foreign-language teaching and aimed to integrate immigrants into the national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Brazilian nationalism historically welcomed immigration; the replacement conspiracy is not part of it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not documented; the Estado Novo abolished elections and corporatist representation replaced party lists.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred: Brazil's nationalism was developmental, not missionary.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from conservative gender hierarchy and not stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Vargas's letter denounces powerful interests and elites against the people; this populist strain is documented but not about corruption per se.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The army applied eugenic criteria to conscripts under Vargas, yet no source shows the nationalist mainstream endorsing state discouragement of reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the regime's torture and repression record and its defence of the military.

night-watchman-state.rationale: State industrial ownership and labour regulation are the opposite.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Miscegenation is the celebrated core of racial democracy, praised by Freyre as democratizing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The racial democracy creed asserts equality, though in practice the regime applied eugenic criteria; formal equality is nationalist rhetoric.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The tradition was anti-communist, so the claim is foreign to it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred: nationalism celebrates Brazil's founding mix and rejects the colonial label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Centralization under Vargas implies uniform national law; religion not specifically addressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Laicity retained in 1937 constitution suggests no restriction.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of Brazilian nationalism; cattle are central to its economy.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Vargas allowed religion in public schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist doctrine not applicable to this tradition.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Split: Vargas claimed popular support while governing without elections; later nationalists accepted electoral consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from import substitution and the aim of reducing dependence; mercantilist leaning.

population-transfer.rationale: Brazilian nationalism sought to integrate not expel minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The regime's own repressive practice and statism reject this libertarian principle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The regime banned the Communist Party and later all parties, under the National Security Law.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Vargas spoke of freedom from foreign domination, but this republican theory is not engaged.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1937 constitution concentrated executive and legislative power in the president.

vanguard-party.rationale: The regime was anti-communist and rejected Leninist vanguardism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Vargas presented himself as defender of "the people and especially the humble."

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council-house sales are a British policy question never raised in the Brazilian nationalist sources, so no lean can be inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The 1937 constitution declared strikes anti-social and removed the right to strike.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred from the developmentalist view that poverty results from underdevelopment.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Brazilian nationalism celebrates diversity in the mixed-race nation as a source of unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rejected by the hierarchical, state-centred tradition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: After the 1935 uprising Vargas secured a state of emergency, suspended civil rights, and used the National Security Law.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the interventionist Vargas state, which fixed coffee prices and intervened in the economy; staple price caps are not documented specifically.

party-controls-media.rationale: The DIP censored newspapers and controlled propaganda; though the state, not a party, did so.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army was a distinct force that deposed Vargas in 1945; the state commands the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Sources describe nationalizing immigrants but give no naturalization period, so adherents cannot be placed on this.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Legislator pay is not discussed in the sources on Vargas-era nationalism; no position is documented.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not documented; Vargas distrusted party factions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1937 constitution concentrated executive power in the president as commander of the forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a nationalist question; the regime only cooperated with the Catholic hierarchy, which is organized by bishops anyway.

clerical-rule.rationale: Laicity was retained and the state led, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Brazil joined the Allies and the movement is patriotic.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The DIP censored media; moral rationale inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Vargas stayed in power by coup and was later elected; unclear doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Brazil joined the Allies and received US financing and bases for CSN.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not a plank and foreign to the tradition.

people-in-arms.rationale: The regime professionalized the armed forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Developmentalism sought to move beyond an agrarian country.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not applicable; Brazil is not divided.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources show no anti-intellectual strand; ISEB itself was an intellectual body, while Vargas distrusted liberal elites, so adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalism celebrates a distinct fusion culture but also stressed whitening in the elite phase.

death-penalty.rationale: The 1937 constitution admitted the death penalty.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-Catholic education stance.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The curriculum fight over evolution is not documented for this tradition; religion in public schools was allowed, but creationism is not mentioned.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the regime's censorship and moral tone.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Brazil's tradition is jus soli, and the regime sought to nationalize immigrants.

minority-language-support.rationale: The nationalization campaign banned teaching in foreign languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The regime favoured uniform national law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the regime's conformist patriotic education.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: ISEB warned of foreign-debt risk but cancellation is not stated.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Vargas described fighting foreign economic domination to create "national freedom" via Petrobras.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Vargas's 1937 constitution was imposed; the 1934 was assembled; split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Estado Novo justified authoritarian rule as readjusting politics to the economic needs of the country.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition rejected foreign dependence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1937 constitution had indirect elections; later nationalists accepted direct election.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Brazil has no territorial dispute of this kind and the sources show no nationalist stance on land-for-peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Nationalists subordinated private interests to national and social good, as in profits limits.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The characterization of the USSR is a Marxist debate; Brazilian nationalists were anti-communist and did not engage in it.

collective-defense.rationale: Brazil joined the Allied war effort, but not a stated doctrine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: No source covers annexation questions; Brazilian nationalism is not irredentist, so no lean is documented.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Vargas cooperated with the Church rather than curbing it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Vargas as father of the nation above parties; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Vargas's national unity centralization ended state autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Propaganda mythologized Vargas but not as divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from statist leanings.

character-from-environment.rationale: Freyre-style culturalism stresses environment and culture over biology.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The 1937 constitution gave Vargas absolute control, though framed as constitutional.

space-expansion.rationale: Space as a civilizational goal postdates the movement's classic period; nothing in the sources bears on it.

leader-cult.rationale: Propaganda aimed to turn Vargas into a myth, the "father of the poor."

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed in the sources on this tradition, so the answer is neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The tradition denied class struggle altogether and was anti-communist, so a debate about socialism's later class struggle is foreign to it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Vargas courted planters and did not break up estates; rural workers were left out.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not part of this tradition's documented concerns.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Brazilian nationalism is territorial, not ethnic irredentist.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a feature in a secular tradition.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Centralization and nationalization campaign denied minority cultural institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Concerns a persecuted minority choosing between rights and emigration; the sources show no Brazilian nationalist view on it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The tradition rejects Marxist historical materialism, though Vargas tied politics to the economic needs of the country.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists favoured state-coordinated industry.

no-bailouts.rationale: The Estado Novo bought and destroyed coffee surpluses to prop up the sector, showing state rescue of key interests.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; the Estado Novo constrained courts through emergency law while keeping judicial autonomy.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Import substitution aimed at industrial self-reliance, though not a closed bloc with colonies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding labour and environmental clauses in trade deals are not discussed; nationalists favoured protection rather than such treaty standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral versus material incentives is a socialist debate; the sources show Vargas-era nationalists relying on wages and state-supervised labour law.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Tenentismo, the military rebel movement, held something like it, but this is not the mainstream doctrine.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Estado Novo education and propaganda centred an authentic Brazilian national culture.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The tradition defines itself against domination by foreign powers.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Estado Novo's nationalization and civic campaign taught national loyalty, with flags and national symbols prominent.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial democracy holds there is little racism, so race-conscious preferences have met resistance from its defenders.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not discussed in the sources; state-led development suggests no strong view either way.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: ISEB sought a national capitalist revolution, believing capitalism could deliver development with state guidance.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not applicable; Portugal's links are secondary.

delink-world-market.rationale: ISEB sought national development by industrialization, not withdrawal from the world market, though it limited foreign capital.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis about rich-country workers; Brazilian nationalists do not take it up in the sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Racial democracy ideology and nationalist state oppose racial discrimination, at least formally.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Vargas said individuals have duties rather than rights, and amended or ignored constitutional limits.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Nationalism arose against Portuguese rule, but nothing in the sources covers the voiding of colonial-era partition treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Split; Vargas accepted both coup rule and elections.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian and order-oriented regime.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Vargas dissolved Congress and concentrated lawmaking in the president.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not documented as a concern of Brazilian nationalists.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use regulation is not discussed in the sources on this tradition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Vargas's paternalist self-presentation as protector of the humble is a related theme.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition demands civic engagement and loyalty.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The regime used mass culture and propaganda itself.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim that the movement does not discuss; its corporatism stressed state organization over cultural hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Vargas lamented decades of domination and spoliation by international economic and financial groups, with foreign profits up to 500% a year.

native-born-offices.rationale: The regime's nationalization stress on Brazilians, including two-thirds of factory jobs, suggests it; exact public-office rule is inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Concerns relations among communist parties, which are not part of this anti-communist nationalist tradition.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Vargas pursued "national freedom" by developing national wealth through Petrobras and Eletrobras against foreign pressure, though foreign loans were also used.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The tradition integrates indigenous people into a mixed nation.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Estado Novo was itself fascist-inspired, though Brazil joined the Allies.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Split; the regime was anti-communist but not anti-fascist.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historiographical dispute with no connection to Brazilian nationalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from cultural nationalism and heritage.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed in any source on this tradition; no basis for a lean either way.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed in any source on this tradition; no basis for a lean either way.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Vargas rejected liberalism as ill-suited to Brazil's conditions, wanting political organism readjusted to the economy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army backed the oil campaign and the Estado Novo, and later deposed Vargas in 1945, a guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognition of unpaid care work is not documented in the Vargas-era sources, which were centred on formal employment.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the family-oriented hierarchical values.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the Estado Novo professionalized administration.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The Petrobras monopoly left no room for foreign participation, and nationalists resisted foreign control of strategic sectors.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: state-linked social insurance was part of the Vargas model.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Use-based tenure is not part of the sources; the regime left planter estates intact, so mild disagreement is inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was dissolved under the Estado Novo.

single-official-language.rationale: Foreign-language teaching was banned and Portuguese was imposed on immigrant regions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the nationalization campaign; restrictions on foreigners are plausible but not documented.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Racial-democracy ideology denies racial discrimination as systemic.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The sources are silent on consumption; developmentalists wanted growth and a national market, so no clear criticism of consumerism.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Brazil did not run a bloc of dependent allies in these sources, so great-power intervention is not a documented question.

corporate-influence.rationale: Vargas's letter blames foreign and national groups' campaign for his fall.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Resistance to foreign influence in the economy and politics is central.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed, though the regime restricted immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not discussed in the sources.

democratic-peace.rationale: A liberal international-relations thesis not engaged by the sources on Vargas-era nationalism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The regime stressed citizens' duties and order.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty against foreign pressure is central, though intervention against others is not discussed.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: Vargas's official unions were organized by occupational category.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Though the regime flirted with xenophobia, Brazilian nationalism had no mainstream conspiracy claim.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The 1937 constitution had a chapter on the family.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not documented; the tradition sought a national, not local, industrial base.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty against international groups is core; constitutional primacy is inferred from it.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by cultural fusion, not religion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist formulation; the sources show no view on personal belongings beyond defence of workers' wages.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism was a defining trait and the regime banned and jailed communists.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources do not discuss delivery models for public services such as mixed provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: The regime drew close to the Church.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: ISEB saw national capitalist development as progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the tradition's economic programme was not framed in terms of women's equality.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The 1943 grammar reform and renaming of clubs (Palmeiras) show linguistic nationalism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties between states and internal nations are not discussed; the tradition integrates indigenous peoples rather than treating them as treaty partners.

majority-settlement.rationale: Immigrant integration policy but not majority settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The corporatist, state-led third course between liberalism and communism was the self-image of the Estado Novo.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historic or religious claims to land are not a Brazilian nationalist theme in the sources.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a position; wartime Brazil allied with the Allies.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The sources do not address this; the regime's conservatism leans toward disapproval but criminalization is not documented.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Estado Novo suppressed opposition and abolished parties, while later nationalists accepted opposition; split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Brazil defined itself against colonial extraction.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine with no connection to Brazilian nationalism, which is secular in the 1937 constitution; the answer is inferred, not sourced.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A jihadist doctrine contrary to Brazilian nationalism's secular state, which kept laicity in 1937; answer is inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The regime favoured state-organized bodies and a strong executive over direct participation in workplaces and communes.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The racial democracy tradition resists it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Corporatist nationalism claimed to transcend left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation is a Marxist notion; Vargas-era nationalists were anti-communist and saw labour as integrated into the nation by corporatism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The 1937 constitution kept laicity, though the regime drew close to the Church; authority is grounded in the nation, not God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules in state institutions are not covered in the sources.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace confidentiality agreements are a modern issue not addressed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mixed economy with labour protection fits the Vargas model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The regime modernized the army and created the Air Force and military academy; abolition is the opposite of its policy.

rich-first.rationale: ISEB developmentalism with leading industrial regions.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Vargas kept neutrality 1939-41, bargaining between blocs.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit is not discussed; Vargas-era nationalists worked through state banks and agencies.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Resistance to financial groups' pressure on the economy, and ISEB's warnings of foreign debt.

property-franchise.rationale: Vargas's regime abolished suffrage but not on property; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept from Lukacs, not used by this anti-communist nationalist tradition.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Vargas complained of campaigns against him, but the statement is Marxist.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The regime ruled partly by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The nation is a racially mixed fusion.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation postdates the classic movement; nothing in the sources bears on it.

open-government-data.rationale: The Estado Novo's DIP censored the press and controlled information, so open records run counter to its practice.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The nationalist ideal celebrates the mixing of peoples, so restricting intermarriage is against it; religion specifically is not discussed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not documented; the nation is inclusive.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly selected deliberative bodies are not part of the corporatist model, which gave voice to organized classes.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not a theme in the sources; the regime simply cooperated with the existing Catholic Church.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the conservative social outlook of the regime and armed forces; no source discusses it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The state allied with the Church.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The regime was a security state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The tradition stresses one unified nation.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: State social protection is the model.

term-limits.rationale: The sources show no term-limit debate; Vargas himself prolonged his rule, which suggests indifference.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid delegation is a digital-age idea alien to this tradition's corporatist, centralized model.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is a recent concern absent from the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The regime's Catholic ties suggest reluctance about women in clerical office; inferred, as sources are silent.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is only touched by the family chapter of the 1937 constitution, with no stance documented in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are not discussed in the sources, though interventionist instincts would not oppose them.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyright are not discussed; the national industrial focus suggests acceptance of the existing regime.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Estado Novo organized youth patriotic movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing of nuclear weapons is not addressed in the sources on this period.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Vargas traded bases for CSN financing, though sovereignty tradition prefers none.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The sources cover no debate on formally recognizing past genocides.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Historians dispute origins; Brazil lacks an ancient origin.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the regime's conservative, hierarchical gender outlook; no source discusses it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist-theory debate with no connection to Brazilian nationalism; inferred from conservative gender outlook.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Vargas himself invoked his sacrifice and blood as a banner.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The sources describe a pragmatic, developmental politics; Vargas's final letter has sacrificial language but not a cosmic struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Concerns a homeland and diaspora in the Zionist sense; Brazilian nationalism has no such structure in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: The state led culture rather than waiting.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is not part of the sources on this tradition.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist-theology criterion not addressed in the sources; the Catholic-leaning regime did not apply it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Preference for national over foreign control is documented, but not majority ethnicity.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Redrawing regions around a single people is not relevant; Brazil is one centralized unit and the nation is mixed.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions were brought under state control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Concerns the definition of socialism, which this anti-communist tradition does not claim to build.

second-chamber.rationale: 1937 constitution included a Federal Council; split.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of the means of production conflicts with the nationalist preference for national state firms and private capital.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Estado Novo ended state autonomy and Vargas said regional problems no longer existed, the opposite of confederation.

family-wage.rationale: The minimum wage was conceived to support a worker's family; the 1937 constitution has family provisions.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in the sources on this tradition.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is a modern topic not addressed by the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Untraceable payments are inconsistent with a regime controlling capital and surveillance; inferred, as sources are silent.

person-over-state.rationale: Vargas: individuals have duties, not rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The regime's closeness to the Catholic Church and Catholic-conservative education suggests a spiritual view of persons; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Biotechnology in agriculture is absent from the sources of the classic period.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form and the environment are not discussed in the sources.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in the mixed nation but not pure race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The sources do not give a doctrine on the use of force; Brazil joined the Allies in a war but pursued no expansion.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The sources describe fear of foreign economic domination, not a partition plot; no such claim is documented.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is not discussed in the sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not part of the developmentalist sources, which prioritized industrial growth.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational environmental duty is not discussed in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not documented for this tradition, whose conservative gender outlook might agree in part but with no source.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Diplomacy by secret treaty was normal in the period; no source shows this movement demanding openness.

capital-controls.rationale: Vargas fought foreign profit extraction and the extraordinary-profits law, and developmentalists limited foreign capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Estado Novo suppressed autonomous armed forces such as the Integralist putsch.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The tradition valued military discipline and Brazil sent an expeditionary force to Italy, so refusing orders is contrary to it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wages were set by the state's labour courts and minimum wage.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Wage top-ups through tax credits are not part of the sources; wages were set through the minimum wage and labour courts.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The tradition favoured a national plan of industrialization rather than competing local economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is not in the sources, which treat resources as national wealth, as in the oil campaign.

sacred-nation.rationale: Vargas's letter invokes sacrifice for the people.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans are not discussed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; Vargas rejected regional problems.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The sources do not address human nature; the Catholic-leaning regime would be sympathetic but no stance is sourced.

public-service-media.rationale: The DIP shows the state controlled media; an independent public broadcaster is not a documented aim.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Brazilian syncretism but not a stated claim.

farm-price-support.rationale: Vargas created the National Coffee Department and bought and destroyed coffee surpluses to support prices.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Brazil had no nuclear weapons in the period, and the sources do not cover the question.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The sources say nothing on women's inheritance; no objection is documented.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic dispute about naming varieties does not arise in Brazilian nationalism, which treats Portuguese as one language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Liability for pollution damage is not discussed in the sources.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs have no role in the Brazilian state described in the sources; the answer is inferred from the centralized constitution.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental priority is not a theme in the sources, which prioritized industrial growth and state authority over liberty.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Nationalization campaign banned foreign-language teaching and promoted Portuguese.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The Estado Novo corporatist model tied unions to the state and banned strikes, and the 1937 Constitution's corporatism implies state-structured compulsory unions; adherents would reject voluntary-only membership.

voter-id.rationale: The sources do not address voter ID, and the Vargas-era nationalists were more concerned with state power than ballot procedure; inferred as split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1937 Constitution declared the state lay and the nationalist tradition stresses a blended national culture, so inferred mild agreement.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Vargas's Estado Novo suspended elections in the name of national unity and development, implying the tradition sees democracy as more than elections; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: The sources do not address sexual morality, and adherents' Catholic-traditional and modernist wings would be split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; the Estado Novo practiced censorship, which suggests acceptance of state control of media, but the tradition is split on modern shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's state-led labor protection model (CLT, minimum wage), which prefers targeted state programs to one cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women got the vote under Vargas in 1932; inferred as agreement, but the sources used do not state it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the tradition celebrates a blended national culture, including its Catholic heritage, and makes no claim about religion oppressing women.

race-social-construct.rationale: Freyre's racial democracy stressed culture and miscegenation over biological division, though it also drew on whitening ideas; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the Vargas-era tradition favoured state agencies in general but had no stated gender agenda.

missingStatements.text: The country's oil and other strategic natural resources should be developed by a state monopoly closed to foreign companies.
missingStatements.rationale: The Petrobras law of 1953 gave the state a monopoly with no foreign participation, the emblem of the oil-is-ours campaign.

missingStatements.text: A nation's identity is best defined by the blending of its different peoples rather than by any single descent.
missingStatements.rationale: Freyre's racial democracy and the Estado Novo presented the fusion of indigenous, African and European cultures as the authentic national culture.

missingStatements.text: Strikes and lockouts should be banned as harmful to national production.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1937 constitution removed the right to strike and the regime set wages through labour courts and official unions.

notes: Strands differ: the Vargas-era authoritarian strand (1937-45) and the democratic labourist and developmentalist strand (PTB, ISEB) would answer democracy and civil-liberty items differently, and left and right nationalisms diverge on race policy and foreign capital. Many answers on social and technology topics are low-confidence inferences.
